free_tier.stated: A free NAT VPS with a shared IPv4 and a dedicated IPv6: 'NAT VPS is almost similar to other VPS but uses the NAT method so that a single IPv4 can be shared to many VPS and then assigns a different port for each user.' The site states 'Full SSH access', 'Unmetered Bandwidth — All data centers provide Unlimited bandwidth' and 'Shared IPv4 — VPS comes with Shared IPv4 and Dedicated IPv6'. No CPU, RAM or disk figure is published on any page read.
free_tier.notes: a third-party review from 2022 reports 450 MB RAM, 3 GB disk and 8 forwarded ports; that is reported, not documented, and is four years old

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a virtual machine, not an object

retention.stated: 'You can renew your VPS at least 3 days before it expires'. The site describes itself as 'Renewable — Extend your server duration to keep your free server online'. The interval a renewal adds is not stated on any page read; a third-party review of 2022 says 'Must renew every 7 days'.
retention.notes: the renewal window is documented as opening 3 days before expiry; the period added is reported only

record.interface_detail: The register page documents SSH access to the VPS, plus a web panel (VPS info, reinstall, reset password, power control) and a web-based terminal at ssh.hax.co.id.
record.tooling: No CLI, SDK or API library is named: the woiden.id register page was read and lists the web panel and web terminal beside plain SSH.
record.chaining: Same composition as Hax: an IPv6-only root box needs an IPv4 front, and the daily renewal is the part that cannot be automated without an external scheduler and stored credentials.

limits.value: the VPS expires and must be renewed, with the renewal window opening 3 days before expiry; the period added is not published
registration requires a Telegram numeric ID, obtained by messaging @HaxTG_bot with /getid

record.limits_note: The instance is reclaimed unless renewed daily, so the server is only always-on while a human logs in every day; a missed weekend loses the machine and its data.
record.binding_note: the machine expires on a short clock that only a human can reset, so it cannot be an always-on node

identity_cost.detail: Registration requires a Telegram ID obtained via bot interaction. No email, card, authorization hold, or identity document is required on the registration form.

record.reliability_note: no reliability event observed; the vendor routes support through a Telegram group and channel

free_tier.stated: Unmetered Bandwidth: all data centers provide unlimited bandwidth. Shared IPv4: a NAT VPS shares one IPv4 and assigns a different port for each user. [vendor page]

egress.terms: Unmetered bandwidth, stated on the vendor page.; ingress: udp

record.interface_detail: SSH with root and a web panel with console, reinstall and port request.
record.tooling: ssh, wg-quick; the panel issues the public port range
record.chaining: Full root means WG terminates here and a conf is generated locally, so this is an ingress endpoint plus relay in one free box.
record.binding_note: Unmetered bandwidth means no byte quota exists, so nothing in the volume sense fails at 1 TiB/month. What stops a month-long run is the 7-day instance life: miss one renewal and the machine and its address are gone. The vocabulary has no kind for instance lifetime, so retention-clamped carries it, with the caveat that the vendor discloses the 7 days rather than clamping silently.

identity_cost.detail: Registration plus a Telegram account for the renewal code; the renewal flow sends a code through Telegram and adds an arithmetic captcha.

record.reliability_note: Third-party write-ups record the provider's NAT VPS being unusable during outages; a missed 7-day renewal deletes the instance and its address.
record.confidence_note: Unmetered bandwidth and the shared-IPv4 model are on the vendor page today; the port count and 7-day renewal come from third-party write-ups.

evidence.proved: unmetered bandwidth at all data centers, shared IPv4 with a port per user
public port request uses iptables to pass data from the public IP to the VPS
a shared-IPv4 port range is issued per VPS

record.notes: The best volume story in the sweep: unlimited bandwidth, full root, no card. Against it: 7-day manual renewal through a Telegram code, a 8-10 port shared IPv4, and a history of the provider's servers going down. The no-hardware premise is satisfied because this is a rented-free VM, not owned iron.

extras.wg_detail: A full root VPS with a dedicated IPv6 and a DNAT port range on a shared IPv4; WireGuard can be installed and a peer conf generated on the box. The vendor panel forwards 'data from public ip address to your vps' by iptables without naming a protocol.
extras.volume_stated: Unmetered bandwidth, stated on the vendor page.
extras.transit_note: The provider's European hosts carry the traffic.
